Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this call last week. We've pulled together a conservative demand forecast for Q3/Q4 (attached) and want to align on a Dedicated pool plan tied to the enterprise contract we're discussing (DEAL-10234). High-level asks:

- We expect peak steady-state of ~1,800 A8000-equivalent GPUs by Nov 2027, with staged needs starting Sep (600), Oct (+700), Nov (+500).
- OEM quoted lead times for new SKUs are being reported in the market at ~14-18 weeks; our procurement team wants clarity on delivery windows and any ability for staged shipments.
- If OEM timing is tight, we want to understand Redwood's cloud capacity cushions (reserved instances or short-term burst) and pricing for month-to-month bridging.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a staggered delivery plan (tranches) and what vendor coordination you can manage (OEM slot reservation, RMA cadence)? Also attaching our forecast and the procurement contact (procurement@picturalabs.com).

Appreciate a plan outline and any initial numbers/cost delta.

Thanks for flagging, Hannah. Quick proposal based on the forecast and current OEM signals:

Recommended tranche plan (A8000-equivalent):
- Tranche 1 (Sep target): 600 units — source: reserved OEM allocation (slot reservation) + 2-week staging for racking.
- Tranche 2 (Oct target): 700 units — mixed OEM + cloud commit for a 60/40 split (OEM 420 / cloud 280) to reduce lead risk.
- Tranche 3 (Nov target): 500 units — OEM heavy, fulfillment by OEM backlog release.

Estimated OEM lead-times (current quotes): 14-20 weeks depending on SKU and shipping lane. I attached the most recent OEM quote we just received (NVIDIA A8000 tranche pricing and lead-time assumptions).

Short-term bridge: Our cloud partner can provide reserved burst seats (preemptible-equivalent) for up to 400 A8000-eq units on 30- to 90-day contracts. Pricing delta (very rough): +18-26% per token-hour vs OEM-hosted nodes given premium for short window. We'll refine once procurement confirms exact SKU.

Risks and mitigations:
- OEM queue shifts: negotiate slot reservation + partial prepayment to secure queue position.
- Customs/shipping: carve out a 2-week buffer and stagger shipments across two ports.
- Onboarding/PKI: ensure Private deployment key exchange is scheduled in tranche 1 onboarding window to avoid delay.

See attached: OEM_quote_NVIDIA-A8000-2048units.pdf and a one-page provisioning phases doc. I'll coordinate an OEM cadence call if you want.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head, Capacity Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OEM_quote_NVIDIA-A8000-2048units.pdf; Redwood_provisioning-phases.pdf

Adding a few engineering/ops constraints to Ben's plan:

1) SKU flexibility: If Pictura can accept a mixed SKU lane (e.g., A8000 + A6000-like equivalents with quantization profiles) we gain ~4-6 weeks of scheduling flexibility. Suggest we present a 3-option menu (all-A8000 / mixed-SKU / hybrid cloud-heavy).

2) Staggered onboarding: Tranche 1 must include a small pilot (48-72 GPUs) for integration testing and KV-cache warmup. That pilot should be part of the Sep shipment so we can validate model latency and cost before full-scale rollouts.

3) Vendor cadence ask: We'll request a weekly OEM status digest (ETA updates + serial batches) and a single point of contact at the OEM for slot escalation. We should also push for partial shipments with individual tracking numbers so customs delays don't block entire tranches.

I'll work with infra procurement to draft the slot reservation language (12-weeks notice + 20% deposit or mutually agreed terms). Happy to join the OEM call.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — thanks for the forecast and patience while we pulled options together. Summary of our recommended path tied to DEAL-10234:

1) Staged delivery lanes: Sept (600) / Oct (+700) / Nov (+500). We propose a three-option commitment menu:
   - Option A (OEM-first): all OEM A8000, best-effort slot reservation.
   - Option B (Mixed SKU): 60% A8000 + 40% compatible SKUs to shorten lead.
   - Option C (Hybrid bridge): heavier short-term cloud commitments in Oct (up to 400 units) to guarantee peak coverage while OEM backlog clears.

2) Pilot: include a 48-72 GPU pilot in Tranche 1 for integration and KV-cache warmup.

3) Procurement terms we recommend: 12-week initial notice for slot reservation with 20% deposit on tranche 1 to secure OEM queue. Partial-shipment allowed.

4) Next steps:
   - Please confirm which option you prefer by Mon, 31 May.
   - If Option A or B: procurement to sign the slot reservation SOW (DocuSign link below).
   - If Option C: we'll issue a bridge pricing addendum for cloud-month commitments while OEM fulfillment completes.

I've attached the OEM quote and our provisioning phases doc. Ben and Karthik are on the thread for any technical or cadence questions.
